newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: UKIO MAKES 1996 LOSS, SAYS 1997 IMPROVES.
newsitem.headline: UKIO MAKES 1996 LOSS, SAYS 1997 IMPROVES.

text.p: Ukio Bankas said it made a loss in 1996 and assets decreased after the country's bank crisis but that the first two months of 1997 showed positive developments.
The bank said in a statement after a shareholder meeting on Saturday that the net loss of the bank in 1996 was 7.7 million litas after it made special provisions of 12.1 million litas for bad loans.
"The ultimate goal for this year thus is to lay a solid foundation for future earnings growth," the bank said.
"The first two months of the current financial year have indicated that the bank is experiencing positive operational and financial developments," it said.
Total assets fell to 197.3 million litas from 240.4 million litas. The bank said the asset fall was due to efforts to improve the quality of services rather than trying to expand.
Gross loans were 152 million litas versus 201 million litas at the end of 1995 and no loans were extended in the second half of the year, the bank said.
It said it made provisions worth 44 million litas versus 22.8 million litas in 1995 and interest was no longer being accrued on 70 million litas of gross loans.

Total provisions were 29 percent of gross loans versus 11.4 percent in 1995. It said the provisions were higher as an examination of the loan portfolio showed related party lending to three distinct commercial groups.
Deposits fell by 22 percent or 40.6 million litas to 146.15 million litas.
